subject: orthopaedics
title: Shoulder and elbow: cuffs, frozen capsules and tennis elbows

steps.tx: The **supraspinatus** starts abduction and tears most often, producing a painful arc between sixty and one twenty degrees. A **drop arm** sign suggests a massive tear, while the empty can test of **Jobe** provokes weakness and pain. Magnetic resonance imaging grades tear size, retraction and fatty change before repair. Cuff centering physiotherapy restores function for many partial tears without surgery.
steps.say: The top cuff tendon will begin the movement that lifts the arm away from the body. A tear makes the middle range of lifting painful and weak in many patients. Letting the raised arm fall suddenly suggests a large and complete tendon tear. Imaging then measures tear size and how far the tendon has pulled back. Strengthening the remaining cuff muscles restores control for many smaller tears.

steps.tx: This coronal scan shows a bright **full thickness tear** of the supraspinatus tendon with retraction and wasting of its muscle belly. The labelled **humeral head** and tendon gap make the level of injury easy to follow. The image matters because tear size and muscle atrophy guide the choice between physiotherapy and repair. For the exam, link this tendon with initiation of abduction and a painful arc.
steps.say: The scan shows a bright gap where the main lifting tendon should attach to bone. The tendon end has pulled away from the head of the arm bone. Its muscle belly looks shrunken because chronic disuse and tear cause wasting over time. Those details help the surgeon judge whether repair can succeed mechanically. Examiners use this view to test tendon anatomy and tear recognition together.

vis.alt: Coronal shoulder MRI showing full thickness supraspinatus tear with retraction and muscle belly wasting.
vis.caption: Shoulder MRI showing supraspinatus tear with muscle atrophy. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Impingement** follows the Neer stages from oedema through fibrosis to spur formation under the acromion. A hooked **Bigliani** acromion narrows the outlet and rubs the cuff with each lift. **Calcific tendinitis** deposits hydroxyapatite that aches sharply during its resorptive phase, and needling with lavage can help. Night pain when lying on that side is a classic complaint.
steps.say: The space above the cuff narrows and pinches the tendon during arm elevation. Disease advances from swelling through scarring to a bony spur under the shoulder blade tip. A hooked bone shape leaves less room and worsens the mechanical rubbing. Chalky deposits inside the tendon cause sudden severe pain when they resorb. Steroid placed into that space settles many painful episodes effectively.

steps.tx: **Frozen shoulder** passes through freezing, frozen and thawing phases, and diabetes makes it bilateral and prolonged. The capsular pattern limits external rotation most, then abduction and internal rotation. Most cases resolve over about **eighteen months**, although stiffness can linger beyond that time. **Hydrodilatation** stretches the capsule, and manipulation or arthroscopic release serves resistant cases.
steps.say: The shoulder capsule thickens and tightens until almost every movement becomes restricted. Turning the arm outward fails first and most severely in the typical pattern. Diabetes makes the problem last longer and affect both sides more often. Many shoulders will loosen slowly over many months without any surgical procedure. Stretching the capsule with fluid helps selected patients who stay stiff.

steps.tx: **Tennis elbow** affects the extensor origin, and the Cozen and Mill tests reproduce lateral pain at the elbow. **Golfer elbow** affects the medial flexor origin instead, as this diagram contrasts across the joint. A **counterforce brace** and eccentric loading form the base of treatment for both. Cubital tunnel disease tingles the little finger, while a distal biceps rupture gives a Popeye deformity.
steps.say: The diagram will gather the common painful conditions around one elbow joint. Overuse of the wrist extensors causes pain on the outer side of the elbow. Overuse of the flexor group instead causes pain on the inner side. A forearm band reduces pull at the painful tendon origin during activity. Gradual eccentric exercise rebuilds tendon strength over the following weeks.
